stem: Join: "Many students work part-time. These students often have less time to study."
choices: Students who work part-time often have less time to study.
Students which work part-time often have less time to study.
Students, who work part-time, they often have less time to study.
Students work part-time who often have less time to study.
explanation: Use who for people, with no extra pronoun.

stem: Join: "The city has a new metro. The metro opened in 2022."
choices: The city has a new metro, which opened in 2022.
The city has a new metro, that opened in 2022.
The city has a new metro which it opened in 2022.
The city has a new metro, who opened in 2022.
explanation: After a comma, use which, not that.

stem: Which sentence correctly expresses an unlikely situation?
choices: If public transport were free, more people would use it.
If public transport is free, more people would use it.
If public transport were free, more people will use it.
If public transport would be free, more people use it.
explanation: Second conditional: if + past, would + verb.

stem: Which sentence correctly expresses a likely result?
choices: If the government invests in schools, standards will rise.
If the government will invest in schools, standards rise.
If the government invested in schools, standards will rise.
If the government invests in schools, standards would have risen.
explanation: First conditional: if + present, will + verb.

stem: Join: "The report was published in 2020. It changed government policy."
choices: Published in 2020, the report changed government policy.
Publishing in 2020, the report changed government policy.
Published in 2020, government policy was changed by it.
The report published in 2020, it changed government policy.
explanation: A past participle clause describes the subject of the main clause.

stem: Join: "Many people want to save money. They cook at home."
choices: Wanting to save money, many people cook at home.
Wanted to save money, many people cook at home.
Wanting to save money, cooking at home is popular.
Many people want to save money, cook at home.
explanation: The -ing clause must describe the subject that follows.

stem: Join: "Electric cars are expensive. Sales are rising."
choices: Although electric cars are expensive, sales are rising.
Despite electric cars are expensive, sales are rising.
Although electric cars are expensive, but sales are rising.
Electric cars are expensive although sales, are rising.
What concerns many parents is the cost of childcare.
What concerns many parents it is the cost of childcare.
That concerns many parents is the cost of childcare.
What does concern many parents the cost of childcare.
explanation: A what-clause can be the subject.

stem: Rewrite in a formal, impersonal style: "People believe that the plan will fail."
choices: It is believed that the plan will fail.
It believes that the plan will fail.
The plan is believing to fail.
It is believe the plan will fail.
explanation: It is believed that is a common academic structure.

choices: Not only does exercise improve health, but it also boosts mood.
Not only exercise improves health, but it also boosts mood.
Not only does exercise improves health, but also mood.
Not only exercise does improve health, it also boosts mood.
It is the cost that prevents many people from studying abroad.
It is the cost what prevents many people from studying abroad.
The cost it is that prevents studying abroad.
It is the cost prevents many people from studying abroad.
explanation: It is ... that ... emphasises one element.

stem: Join: "Some countries have high taxes. These countries tend to have good public services."
choices: Countries with high taxes tend to have good public services.
Countries with high taxes they tend to have good public services.
Countries which high taxes tend to have good public services.
High taxes countries tending to have good services.
explanation: A short prepositional phrase can replace a relative clause.

choices: The more people use cars, the worse congestion becomes.
More people use cars, worse congestion becomes.
The more people use cars, the more worse congestion becomes.
The more people use cars, congestion becomes worse the.

stem: Join: "Cities are building cycle lanes. They want to reduce traffic."
choices: Cities are building cycle lanes in order to reduce traffic.
Cities are building cycle lanes for reduce traffic.
Cities are building cycle lanes so as reducing traffic.
Cities are building cycle lanes for to reduce traffic.

stem: Join: "The factory closed. Then many workers moved away."
choices: After the factory closed, many workers moved away.
After the factory closed, so many workers moved away.
The factory closed after many workers moved away.
After closing the factory, many workers moved away.
explanation: After + clause keeps the order of events clear. The last option wrongly suggests the workers closed it.

choices: The town where I grew up has changed a lot.
The town which I grew up has changed a lot.
The town where I grew up in has changed a lot.
The town that I grew up there has changed a lot.
explanation: Where = in which; no extra in or there.

stem: Which sentence correctly talks about the past?
choices: If the city had built more homes, prices would not have risen so fast.
If the city built more homes, prices would not have risen so fast.
If the city had built more homes, prices will not rise so fast.
If the city would have built more homes, prices did not rise.
explanation: Third conditional: if + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

choices: While online courses are flexible, they require strong self-discipline.
While online courses are flexible, but they require self-discipline.
Online courses while flexible require, self-discipline.
While online courses flexible, they require self-discipline.
explanation: While + full clause, then the main clause, with no but.
